While Telemachus is in play no gladiator can attack. Each player rolls a d6 at the start of their turn; a 1 or 6 drags him out. Use the lull to break pots? No: pots need attacks too. Move, loot, trade, buy and reposition instead.
For the next 4 turns, any gladiator who ends a turn without attacking gets every gladiator stoned for 2 damage. Hit something, even a pot, every turn.
From now on every attack rolls 4 hit dice and the attacker chooses the hit location. Fights end quickly: armor your head and chest, and go for the weakest location on your rivals.
For one full turn rotation, each gladiator rolls a d6 at the start of their Resolve phase. Odd means the boar deals 2 damage to a rolled location.

A beast you attack or push becomes aggro on you: it follows you anywhere and attacks during your Resolve phase. Each NPC holds only one aggro target, the most recent gladiator to hit it. It still lashes out at anyone standing next to it. Tunnels, a Ward of the Evil Eye or a Meat Lure shake it off.
You have 2 turns of grace to get inside the lit zone. Ending a turn outside costs 2 CF, and negative CF eliminates you.

Raising your grades: treasury and low greed raise Coin; wins and fame raise Glory and Spectacle; Discipline plus improved fighters raises Training; a small roster raises Arena time; and Honor is the slow one — poaches (−9) and broken pledges (−6) scar it, kept pledges (+3) heal it.

The tools: Pitch (1h, aimed at a motive you grade well), Send a gift (2h, lands hardest on coin-hungry fighters), Host a feast (4h, the big swing), Scout (3h, sparring report + motives), and the Pledge — promise the main event within 2 weeks for +12 interest at the table. Keep it and the barracks notice; break it and your Honor pays for years.

Fates in the league. Every league bout ends the way a board-game event does: each fighter meets the Fate table (p.54-55). Under 17 CF they are condemned (Damnatio or a Fatal Charade); 17-19 CF, the Thumb of Flavius — you roll the d6 yourself on Match Week (4-6 spares them, 1-3 hands them to a d12 death); 20-49 CF, the Ludus Flavius — they survive; 50+ CF, the rudis — freedom, theirs to take (you can ask them to stay). Any condemned fighter can be bought back with blood money paid to the editor — the price rises with their rating, fame and how grim the sentence. (A missio, in Flavius Rule, is something else entirely: a five-event campaign for one gladiator — see New event → Missio.)

How fighters enter the league: two or three new faces arrive every week (mostly rookies, 17–21, low-rated but high-potential and cheap); your arena's saved Ludus Flavius gladiators and Creator Studio characters join every new career; and a bout short of entrants conscripts a fresh sword on the spot.

How they leave: death under the thumb; two severed limbs (unless healed by Hygeia); a cheap free agent who goes unsigned ~14 weeks gives up and goes home; and age — every season is a birthday, and past 35 each year makes hanging up the sword likelier.

Age shapes class: the young arrive mostly as Slaves and Soldiers; the graying re-badge as Veteranus. Mid-career (23–31) is when fighters most often change class — at a ludus's request, after new drills, on an omen-reader's advice, or plain restlessness. The news criers report every change.
Royalty leans lucky: Luck 76+ pays coin each turn. Bank it into level 2-3 weapons; the Pugio hits for 2.
Slaves lean fast: Speed 76+ means an extra tile a turn to race to pots and away from beasts; the Rete stops a chaser.

Accept invitations you can win. The stars are honest: a ★★★ Leptis Cup is a fine first trophy; the ★★★★★ Colossus draws the league's best. Two fighters in the Colossus means two heats with a chance — they never meet in round one.

The Medicus, the surgeon and Hygeia's priests also count toward your physicians' weekly cap — they can do at most {0} coin of treasury a week ({1} left this week); the bathhouse and the temple of Asclepius are outside help and do not count. Care must match the wound: rest heals bruises, the Medicus mends muscle, only the surgeon's knife stops a festering wound, and only Hygeia regrows a lost limb. Ignore a festering wound for three weeks and your fighter dies, flees, or is never quite whole again.
The steam room sits empty; the surgeon sharpens his knives on nothing. May it stay that way.
